threads.body: [General] Avoid logging the complete `ioreg` response here. `IOPlatformExpertDevice` output also includes `IOPlatformSerialNumber` and other hardware identifiers, so the missing-UUID path can disclose them when FINE logging is enabled; log only that the lookup failed.

Any reason this is a `String[]` instead of a list like the constants above?

```suggestion
  private static final List<String> WINDOWS_ROOT_ENV_VARS = asList("SystemRoot", "windir");
```

Now that there's a `commandExecutor`, can we drop the `queryWindowsRegistry` supplier and have `readWindowsGuid()` use `commandExecutor` like macOS and BSD do? That's one less constructor param, no more `null, null` in the tests, and it makes `windowsRegPath()` testable.

semconv#3896 only added full paths for the BSD `kenv` and macOS `ioreg` rows -- the Windows row still just says "MachineGuid from registry", so this part is new behavior for all Windows users and has no test coverage (`createResourceWindows` injects `queryWindowsRegistry`, so `windowsRegPath()` never runs).

Can we get a test for it?

`runCommand` has no timeout. That was already true, but it mattered less when only Windows used it -- now macOS runs it on the default path, so a stuck `ioreg` would hang SDK startup.

Note it isn't just adding `waitFor(timeout, unit)`: `getProcessOutput` blocks on EOF before we ever reach `waitFor`, so the read needs to be bounded too. Fine as a follow-up.

`runningLinux()` and `runningMacOs()` both lowercase before matching, but this one is case-sensitive. It happens to work for every real `os.name` (`FreeBSD`, `OpenBSD`, `NetBSD`, `DragonFly BSD`), so this is just for consistency.

```suggestion
    return getOsType.get().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).endsWith("bsd");
```

Nit: the lambda can just be a method reference (only the one-arg `System.getenv(String)` overload is applicable here).

```suggestion
    command.add(windowsRegPath(System::getenv));
```
